mechanism: Both drugs are nephrotoxic with dose-dependent renal impairment; foscarnet causes electrolyte abnormalities (hypocalcemia, hypomagnesemia) and tenofovir causes proximal tubule dysfunction, resulting in cumulative nephrotoxicity and reduced clearance of both agents.
action: Monitor serum creatinine, electrolytes, and urinalysis frequently; maintain adequate hydration; consider dose adjustment or alternative agents if renal function declines; assess risk-benefit ratio given both drugs target CMV/HIV in immunocompromised patients.
